Company Description

Everyone’s story matters. Come shape your story with us at Riverty.
But where does that take you?

To one of our 30 hybrid workspaces – designed for exchanging ideas, learning from others, and shaping the way we work. An international community of over 4,000 people, representing almost 80 nationalities across 11 countries. United by one mission: Combining empathy, advanced technology and data-driven insights to keep people and businesses in flow. With payments made for them. So that they don’t have to worry about it.

And there’s more. We are part of the family-owned Bertelsmann group. Established. Corporate. In a fast-paced industry. We enable flexible payments in various industries, simplifying the financial management of known brands and helping people repay debt to build financial confidence. In short: shaping FinTech.

Job Description

We are looking for a

Finance Process Manager (m/f/d)

(permanent, full-time) Join our team at our location in Münster, Varberg or Verl - flexible working conditions available

Your tasks:

- As part of a team of eight within Operational Finance, you Collaborate with cross-functional and multidisciplinary teams within BU Pay & Credit to implement process changes.
- Act as the main point of contact for new products within Operational Finance CBS, ensuring the correct design and implementation of finance processes across all countries.
- Support and contribute to efficient General Ledger (GL) processes.
- Take ownership of the GL setup as a Subject Matter Expert, driving product innovations and continuous improvements.
- Design and model digital accounting and booking processes and translate them into clear system requirements.
- Act as the key interface for operational and financial topics between Operational Finance, IT, platform teams, and other relevant stakeholders.

Qualifications

Your Profil:

- You have successfully completed a degree in business administration, business mathematics, business informatics or comparable training with relevant professional experience
- You have practical experience in financial management
- You have strong analytical and conceptual skills as well as problem-solving skills
- You combine a keen interest in IT with strong Microsoft 365 skills
- You enjoy communicating confidently in written and spoken English

Additional Information

Disclosure requirements pertaining to the collection of your personal data:

Responsible for processing the information provided in your application is the company specified in the job advertisement, with its registered office as indicated. The company processes your data for the purpose of establishing an employment relationship on the basis of Art. 6 (1) b GDPR / Section 26 (1) sentence 1 BDSG.

The retention period for your data is determined by the statutory time limits applicable in the respective country, beginning upon completion of the recruitment process. You can find these here (https://bertelsmann-hr.de/docs/Overview_of_Data_Retention_Periods_EN.pdf) .

You can contact the company’s Data Protection Officer at the above-mentioned postal address.

We are looking for a motivated Bioinformatics Data Steward (m/f/d) to support our Data Management unit in the Bioinformatics Department at TRON. You will further develop and implement solutions for efficient organization and coordination of diverse types of research data across multiple projects.

As part of our team, you will have the opportunity to work with talented and dedicated colleagues, to develop and expand your professional expertise, and to be at the cutting-edge of translational science to improve patient lives.

Bioinformatics / DATA Steward (m/f/d)
Full time - Mainz
Ensure data quality, integrity, consistency and regulatory compliance, while managing data in accordance with the FAIR principles.
Collaborate with scientists, software developers, machine learning engineers, and IT teams on efficient data management standards.
Organize and annotate large scale and multi-dimensional research datasets (genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, clinical metadata, etc.).
Manage data access and download from, and data submission to repositories such as EGA, ENA, dbGAP, etc.
Provide guidance and training on data stewardship and data management best practices.

M.Sc. in Bioinformatics or a comparable field, supplemented by a minimum of 2 years of professional working experience.
Experience in research data management in bioinformatics or life sciences.
Knowledge of FAIR principles, metadata standards, and data stewardship best practices.
Experience with databases, scientific repositories, and scripting languages (e.g., Python or R).
Strong organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a multidisciplinary research environment.
An excellent command of English.
Enthusiasm and curiosity for the diverse activities of our research institute as well as the ability to work in a team completes your profile.

A dynamic, innovative and creative research environment
An open, collegial and cordial working atmosphere in a respectful corporate culture
A high degree of diversity in the workforce
Performance-related remuneration and other benefits
The opportunity for personalised further training TRON - Translational Oncology at the University Medical Center of the Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz non-profit GmbH

jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com
The Position
As a Senior Clinical Program Leader, you will play a pivotal role in advancing innovative therapies for patients living with obesity and liver diseases. Working at the forefront of clinical development, you will lead cross-functional teams, drive early-stage clinical programs from strategy through execution and contribute to critical development and regulatory decisions. This is a unique opportunity to combine scientific excellence, strategic leadership, and patient-focused innovation to make a meaningful impact on global healthcare.
Join us in shaping the future of medicine and apply now!
Tasks & responsibilities

- In your new role, you will design and prepare clinical development plans, focusing on Phase I and II in Obesity & Liver indications.
- You will guide cross-functional teams, including experts from clinical trial operations, biostatistics, biomarkers, and patient safety, to ensure high-quality execution as the clinical lead.

- You will provide input to regulatory strategy and clinical components of briefing documents, presentations, and responses to questions.
- Moreover, you will contribute to the Medical Affairs strategy and deliverables, including key documents such as the Integrated Evidence Plan, in collaboration with Medical Advisor(s) and the Medical Affairs Lead.
- You will leverage your clinical expertise to evaluate external opportunities and support decisions that strengthen the pipeline.
- In addition, you will supervise and mentor other Clinical Program Leads within the assigned program/asset, while serving as a delegate for the Clinical Development Lead in designated tasks and responsibilities, as required.

Requirements

- Strong leadership skills with the ability to lead and motivate cross-functional teams

The purpose of the Specialist Regional Risk Management is to manage, coordinate and drive all profit protection related topics in region, including data analysis and reporting. - You will support the creation and update of internal policies, procedures, and operational guidelines related to loss prevention and profit protection

- You will provide practical support and solutions to all stores on high incident levels or elevated risk

- You will deliver training to store teams on loss prevention practices, risk awareness, and emergency procedures
- You will conduct regular audits to monitor compliance with loss prevention policies and follow up on any findings

- University degree in business, economics, textile or related fields - or comparable education with relevant work experience
- Previous experience in profit protection, ideally gained within a retail environment
- Ability to research and analyze multiple data streams to make informed decisions
- Knowledge of store processes and procedures
- Strong project and time management skills with excellent attention to detail
- Knowledge of local/ regional store processes, laws & regulations and cultural needs
- Very good analytical skills, as well as advanced knowledge in Microsoft Excel and SAP BW
- Independent, highly structured and precise way of working
- Professional and authentic appearance & communication, discreet workstyle
- Willingness to travel if necessary      
- Fluent in both written and spoken English and German

jobs.employer_name: Rheinland-Pfälzische Techn. Univers. Kaiserslautern-Landau Standort Landau
jobs.description:
With about 15,000 students, more than 300 professorships and around 160 degree programs, the RPTU University Kaiserslautern-Landau is the technical university of the state of Rhineland-Palatinate. As a place of top international research, it offers excellent working conditions and career opportunities. Those who study, research or work at RPTU experience a cosmopolitan environment and shape the future.

The position will be part of young research group with a focus on hydrologic process analysis and hydrologic extremes. We use large sample datasets, spatially extensive models and comprehensive literature extraction to gain knowledge on hydrologic behaviour across different spatio-temporal scales. The position is part of the Carl-Zeiss project “AI4ChemRisk” (AI for Chemical Risk Prediction in Aquatic Environments) collaborating with leading research groups in AI, Machine-Learning and Environmental Data Science at the RPTU and abroad.

Your area of responsibility:

- extraction of hydrologic process knowledge from the scientific literature using large language models and natural language processing
- work with sample hydrological data to combine hydrologic process knowledge with chemical risk data
- prediction of hydrological risk factors for aquatic chemical risk
- stakeholder engagement, outreach and collaboration

Your requirements profile:

Applicants should hold an excellent bachelor’s and master’s degree (or equivalent) in hydrology, water resources, or any closely‑related environmental science or in computer science, data science, statistics, or applied mathematics provided they have a demonstrated interest in hydrological processes. Candidates from other quantitative or earth‑system disciplines (e.g., geography, atmospheric science, ecology, civil‑environmental engineering, remote sensing, GIS, environmental physics) are also encouraged to apply if they can show relevant coursework or research experience.

We are looking for a motivated and curious researcher who has

- strong programming proficiency (Python, R, MATLAB, or similar). Experiences with NLP, LLM or high‑performance computing is a plus.
- enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research and collaboration within an international team
- excellent analytical and problem-solving skills
- strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken
- motivation to publish high-quality scientific research and complete a PhD within three years
- work in a motivated, innovative team focusing on data-driven hydrology
- close supervision and individualized mentoring to support your scientific and professional development
- integration into various hydrological research tasks of national to global scopes
- an inspiring, collaborative, and international research environment with strong interdisciplinary interactions
- integration into established national and international research networks and opportunities to present your work at leading scientific conferences
- flexible work environment

RPTU stands for diversity among all employees. We welcome applications from all interested parties, regardless of their ethnic and social origin, age, religion, gender, disability and sexual orientation or identity. Preference will be given to severely disabled persons and persons equivalent to them if they have the appropriate qualifications and suitability.

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

The Clinical Diagnostics Division (CDD) provides innovative diagnostic solutions across selected in vitro diagnostics (IVD) market segments and has been a trusted partner to the IVD industry for more than 40 years.

Our portfolio includes solutions for drugs-of-abuse testing, therapeutic drug monitoring, quality control, sepsis diagnosis, prenatal screening and more. In addition, CDD offers advanced laboratory instrumentation and high-throughput automation solutions for a wide range of clinical laboratory environments.

Our products and solutions are delivered through direct sales, regional distributors and OEM partnerships.

As a trusted advisor to clinical laboratories and healthcare customers, you will combine your scientific understanding with a consultative sales approach to identify customer needs, understand laboratory workflows and develop solutions that deliver measurable value.

- Represent Thermo Fisher Scientific at customer meetings, industry events, conferences and exhibitions
- Ensure high levels of customer satisfaction and develop sustainable, long-term business partnerships

Keys to Success

You combine a strong scientific or technical background with commercial drive and a genuine passion for understanding and solving customer challenges.

You are comfortable managing a large territory independently, identifying growth opportunities and engaging with stakeholders at different levels of an organization. At the same time, you enjoy working collaboratively within a global, cross-functional organization.

Education & Experience

- Master’s degree in Life Sciences, Biology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Medical Technology or another relevant scientific discipline
- Minimum 5 years of successful sales experience, preferably within clinical diagnostics, IVD, laboratory solutions, life sciences, medical technology or healthcare
- Proven track record of achieving or exceeding sales targets and developing a sales territory
- Experience managing complex customer relationships and sales cycles
- Experience working with clinical laboratories, hospitals or other diagnostic customers is highly desirable

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

- Excellent consultative selling, communication, presentation and negotiation skills
- Strong commercial mindset with the ability to identify and develop new business opportunities
- Demonstrated ability to build trusted, long-term relationships with customers and key decision-makers
- Strong analytical, strategic planning and territory management capabilities

- Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively within a cross-functional and matrix organization
